transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s right at the top of my agenda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve shipped millions of jobs overseas and we have a strange situation because we have a process in Washington where after you’ve served for a while you cash in, become a foreign lobbyist, make $30,000 a month, then take a leave, work on presidential campaigns, make sure you’ve got good contacts and then go back out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you just want to get down to brass tacks, first thing you ought to do is get all these folks who’ve got these 1-way trade agreements that we’ve negotiated over the years and say fellas, we’ll take the same deal we gave you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And they’ll gridlock right at that point because for example, we’ve got international competitors who simply could not unload their cars off the ships if they had to comply — you see, if it was a 2-way street, just couldn’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have got to stop sending jobs overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: To those of you in the audience who are business people: pretty simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you’re paying $12, $13, $14 an hour for a factory worker, and you can move your factory south of the border, pay $1 an hour for labor, hire a young — let’s assume you’ve been in business for a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got a mature workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Pay $1 an hour for your labor, have no health care — that’s the most expensive single element in making the car.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Have no environmental controls, no pollution controls and no retirement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you don’t care about anything but making money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There will be a job-sucking sound going south.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If the people send me to Washington the first thing I’ll do is study that 2000-page agreement and make sure it’s a 2-way street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One last point here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I decided I was dumb and didn’t understand it so I called a “Who’s Who” of the folks that have been around it, and I said why won’t everybody go south; they said it will be disruptive; I said for how long.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I finally got ’em for 12 to 15 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I said, well, how does it stop being disruptive?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And that is when their jobs come up from a dollar an hour to $6 an hour, and ours go down to $6 an hour; then it’s leveled again, but in the meantime you’ve wrecked the country with these kind of deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We got to cut it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Carole, the thing that saved us in this global economic slowdown has been our exports, and what I’m trying to do is increase our exports.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if indeed all the jobs were going to move south because there are lower wages, there are lower wages now and they haven’t done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I have just negotiated with the president of Mexico the North American Free Trade Agreement — and the prime minister of Canada, I might add — and I want to have more of these free trade agreements, because export jobs are increasing far faster than any jobs that may have moved overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a scare tactic, because it’s not that many.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But any one that’s here, we want to have more jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the way to do that is to increase our exports.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some believe in protection.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t; I believe in free and fair trade, and that’s the thing that saved us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I will keep on as president trying to get a successful conclusion to the GATT Round, the big Uruguay Round of trade which will really open up markets for our agriculture particularly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to continue to work after we get this NAFTA agreement ratified this coming year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to get one with Eastern Europe; I want to get one with Chile.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And free and fair trade is the answer, not protection.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, as I say, we’ve had tough economic times, and it’s exports that have saved us, exports that have built.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to answer the question, because I’ve actually been a governor for 12 years, so I’ve known a lot of people who have lost their jobs because of jobs moving overseas, and I know a lot of people whose plants have been strengthened by increasing exports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The trick is to expand our export base and to expand trade on terms that are fair to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is true that our exports to Mexico, for example, have gone up and our trade deficit has gone down; it’s also true that just today a record high trade deficit was announced with Japan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So what is the answer?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me just mention three things very quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number one, make sure that other countries are as open to our markets as our markets are to them, and, if they’re not, have measures on the books that don’t take forever and a day to implement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number two, change the tax code.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are more deductions in the tax code for shutting plants down and moving overseas than there are for modernizing plant and equipment here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our competitors don’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Emphasize and subsidize modernizing plant and equipment here, not moving plants overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number three, stop the federal government’s program that now gives low-interest loans and job training funds to companies that will actually shut down and move to other countries, but we won’t do the same thing for plants that stay here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So more trade but on fair terms — and favor investment in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No, and here’s why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you exactly why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because the deficit now has been building up for 12 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you exactly what I think can be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we can bring it down by 50% in 4 years and grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I could get rid of it in 4 years in theory on the books now, but to do it you’d have to raise taxes too much and cut benefits too much to people who need them and it would even make the economy worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot will tell you, for example, that the expert he hired to analyze his plan says that it will bring the deficit down in 5 years but it will make unemployment bad for 4 more years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So my view is, sir, you have to increase investment, grow the economy and reduce the deficit by controlling health care costs, prudent reductions in defense, cuts in domestic programs and asking the wealthiest Americans and foreign corporations to pay their fair share of taxes and investing and growing this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I ask everybody to look at my economic ideas and 9 Nobel prize winners and over 500 economists and hundreds of business people, including a lot of Republicans said, this is the way you’ve got to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t grow the economy you can’t get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I can’t foresee all the things that will happen, and I don’t think a president should be judged solely on the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me also say, we’re having an election today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You’ll have a shot at me in 4 years and you can vote me right out if you think I’ve done a lousy job and I would welcome you to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m a little confused here, because I don’t see how you can grow the deficit down by raising people’s taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I don’t think the American people are taxed too little.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think they’re taxed too much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I went for one tax increase and when I make a mistake I admit it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I said that wasn’t the right thing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton’s program wants to tax more and spend more — $150 billion in new taxes, spend another $220.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe that’s the way to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Here’s some thing that’ll help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Give us a balanced budget amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He always talks about Arkansas having a balanced budget and they do, but he has a balanced budget amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Have to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d like the government to have that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think it would discipline not only the Congress, which needs it, but also the executive branch.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to have what 43 governors have — the line item veto, so if the Congress can’t cut, and we’ve got a reckless spending Congress, let the president have a shot at it by wiping out things that are pork barrel or something of that nature.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve proposed another one.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some sophisticates think it may be a little gimmicky.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a check- off.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says to you as a taxpayer — say you’re going to pay a tax of 1000 bucks or something.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can check 10% of that if you want to, in the 1 box, and that 10%, $100, or if you’re paying $10,000, whatever it is, $1000, check it off and make the government, make it lower the deficit by that amount.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if the Congress won’t do it, if they can’t get together and negotiate how to do that, then you’d have a sequester across the board.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’d exempt Social Security — I don’t want to tax or touch Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m the president that said hey, don’t mess with Social Security, and we haven’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I believe that we need to control the growth of mandatory spending, back to this gentleman’s question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the main growing thing in the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The program that the president — two-thirds of the budget, I as president never get to look at, never get to touch.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to control that growth to inflation and population increase, but not raise taxes on the American people now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t believe that would stimulate any kind of growth at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’re $4 trillion in debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re going into debt an additional $1 billion, little more than $1 billion every working day of the year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, the thing I love about it — I’m just a businessman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I was down in Texas taking care of business, tending to my family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This situation got so bad that I decided I’d better get into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The American people asked me to get into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But I just find it fascinating that while we sit here tonight we will go into debt an additional $50 million in an hour and a half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s not the Republicans’ fault, of course, and it’s not the Democrats’ fault.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And what I’m looking for is who did it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, they’re the 2 folks involved so maybe if you put them together, they did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, the facts are we have to fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m here tonight for these young people up here in the balcony from this college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When I was a young man, when I got out of the Navy I had multiple job offers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Young people with high grades can’t get a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: People — the 18- to 24-year-old high school graduates 10 years ago were making more than they are now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In other words, we were down to 18% of them were making — 18- to 24-year- olds were making less than $12,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now that’s up to 40%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And what’s happened in the meantime?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The dollar’s gone through the floor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, whose fault is that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Not the Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Not the Republicans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Somewhere out there there’s an extraterrestrial that’s doing this to us, I guess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And everybody says they take responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Somebody somewhere has to take responsibility for this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Put it to you bluntly, American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you want me to be your president, we’re going to face our problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Weâ€™ll deal with our problems, weâ€™ll solve our problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ll down our debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ll pass on the American dream to our children, and I will not leave our children a situation that they have today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When I was a boy it took 2 generations to double the standard of living.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Today it will take 12 generations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our children will not see the American dream because of this debt that somebody somewhere dropped on us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t have an answer for everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: As you all know, I’ve been buying 30-minute segments to talk about issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And tomorrow night on NBC, from 10:30 to 11 Eastern, we’re going to talk about how you pay the debt down, so we’re going to come right down to that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ll be on again Saturday night, 8 to 9 o’clock on ABC.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So the point is —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Like Jerry Brown, the 800 number.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: — I couldn’t agree with you more, couldn’t agree with you more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I have said again and again and again let’s get off mud wrestling, let’s get off personalities and let’s talk about jobs, health care, crime, the things that concern the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m spending my money — not PAC money, not foreign money, my money — to take this message to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, in the first place, I believe that character is a part of being president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to look at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that has to be a part of a candidate for president or being president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of programs, I’ve submitted, what, 4 different budgets to the US Congress in great detail.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s so heavy they’d give you a broken back.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And everything in there says what I am for.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now I’ve come out with a new agenda for America’s renewal, a plan that I believe really will help stimulate the growth of this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My record on world affairs is pretty well known because I’ve been president for 4 years, so I feel I’ve been talking issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, nobody likes who shot John, but I think the first negative campaign run in this election was by Governor Clinton, and I’m not going to sit there and be a punching bag; I’m going to stand up and say, hey, listen, here’s my side of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But character is an important part of the equation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The other night Governor Clinton raised my — I don’t know if you saw the debate the other night.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You did — suffered through that?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, he raised the question of my father — it was a good line, well rehearsed and well delivered.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he raised the question of my father and said, well, your father, Prescott Bush, was against McCarthy, you should be ashamed of yourself, McCarthyism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember something my dad told me — I was 18 years old going to Penn Station to go on into the Navy, and he said write your mother — which I faithfully did; he said serve your country — my father was an honor, duty and country man; and he said tell the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve tried to do that in public life, all through it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That says something about character.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My argument with Governor Clinton — you can call it mud wrestling, but I think it’s fair to put it in focus is — I am deeply troubled by someone who demonstrates and organizes demonstration in a foreign land when his country’s at war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Probably a lot of kids here disagree with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But that’s what I feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I feel passionately about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m thinking of Ross Perot’s running mate sitting in the jail.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: How would he feel about it?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But maybe that’s generational.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the big argument I have with the governor on this is this taking different positions on different issues — trying to be one thing to one person here that’s opposing the NAFTA agreement and then for it — what we call waffling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I do think that you can’t turn the White House into the Waffle House.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to say what you’re for and you’ve got to —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I get wound up because I feel strongly —

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say first of all to you that I believe so strongly in the question you asked that I suggested this format tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I started doing these formats a year ago in New Hampshire and I found that we had huge crowds because all I did was let people ask questions and I tried to give very specific answers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also had a program starting last year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been disturbed by the tone and the tenor of this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank goodness the networks have a fact check so I don’t have to just go blue in the face anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush said once again I was going to have $150 billion tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Quayle said that all the networks said, that’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’s got over $100 billion of tax cuts and incentives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I’m not going to take up your time tonight, but let me just say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ll have a debate in 4 days and we can talk about this character thing again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the Washington Post ran a long editorial today saying they couldn’t believe Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush was making character an issue and they said he was the greatest quote “political chameleon” for changing his positions of all times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I don’t want to get into that —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Please don’t get into the Washington Post.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s don’t — you don’t have to believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Here’s my point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m not interested in his character.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to change the character of the presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’m interested in what we can trust him to do and what you can trust me to do and what you can trust Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot to do for the next 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think you’re right and I hope the rest of the night belongs to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about programs for children.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it depends how you define it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, I think in general, let’s talk about these issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about the programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But in the presidency, a lot goes into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Caring goes into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not particularly specific.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Strength goes into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not specific.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Standing up against aggression.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not specific in terms of a program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is what a president has to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So in principle, though, I’ll take your point and think we ought to discuss child care or whatever else it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Ross had his hand up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Just no hedges, no ifs, ands and buts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll take the pledge because I know the American people want to talk about issues and not tabloid journalism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I’ll take the pledge and will stay on the issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, just for the record, I don’t have any spin doctors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any speechwriters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Probably shows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I make those charts you see on television.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But you don’t have to wonder if it’s me talking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, what you see is what you get and if you don’t like it, you got two other choices, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to say just one thing now, Ross, in fairness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The ideas I express are mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked on these things for 12 years and I’m the only person up here who hasn’t been part of Washington in any way for the last 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t want the implication to be that somehow everything we say is just cooked up and put in our head by somebody else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I worked 12 years very hard as a governor on the real problems of real people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m just as sick as you are by having to wake up and figure out how to defend myself every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I never thought I’d ever be involved in anything like this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: May I finish?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Very briefly?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t have any foreign money in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any foreign lobbyists on leave in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any PAC money in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 5 million hard-working people who put me on the ballot, and I belong to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And they’re interested in what you’re interested in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I take the pledge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve already taken the pledge on cutting the deficit in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I never got to say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There’s a great young group, Lead or Leave, college students, young people, who don’t want us to spend their money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I took the pledge we’d cut it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll be glad to take a shot at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not sure that — and I can understand if you haven’t seen this, because there’s been a lot of hue and cry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We passed this year the most furthest looking transportation bill in the history of this country since Eisenhower started the interstate highways — $150 billion for improving the infrastructure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That happened when I was president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’m very proud of the way that came about and I think it’s a very, very good beginning.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Like Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot, I am concerned about the deficits and $150 billion is a lot of money, but it’s awful hard to say we’re going to go out and spend more money when we’re trying to get the deficit down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I would cite that as a major accomplishment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We hear all the negatives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you’re president you expect this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everybody’s running against the incumbent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everyone knows that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But here’s something that we can take great pride in because it really does get to what you’re talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our home initiative — our home ownership initiative — HOPE — that passed the Congress is a good start for having people own their own homes instead of living in these deadly tenements.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our enterprise zones, that we hear a lot of lip service about in Congress, would bring jobs into the inner city.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a good program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I need the help of everybody across this country to get it passed in a substantial way by the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When we went out to south central in Los Angeles — some of you may remember the riots there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I went out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I went to a boys’ club.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And everyone of them — the boys’ club leaders, the ministers — all of them were saying pass enterprise zones.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We go back to Washington and very difficult to get it through the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there’s going to be a new Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No one likes gridlock.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s going to be a new Congress because the old one — I don’t want to get this man made at me — but there was a post office scandal and a bank scandal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to have a lot of new members of Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then you can sit down and say, help me do what we should for the cities.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Help me pass these programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sure, but the problem is, you get so many things included in a great big bill that you have to look at the overall good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the problem with our system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you had a line item veto you could knock out the pork.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You could knock out the tax increases and you could do what the people want, and that’s create enterprise zones.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That bill pays for these urban enterprise zones by asking the wealthiest Americans to pay a little more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why he wants to veto it, just like he vetoed an earlier bill this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is not mud slinging.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is fact slinging — a bill earlier this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is facts — that would have given investment tax credits and other incentives to reinvest in our cities, in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it asked the wealthiest Americans to pay a little more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot wants to do the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let me tell you specifically what my plan does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My plan would dedicate $20 billion a year in each of the next 4 years for investments in new transportation, communications, environmental clean-ups and new technologies for the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we would target it especially in areas that have been either depressed or which have lost a lot of defense related jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are 200,000 people in California, for example, who have lost their defense related jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They ought to be engaged in making high speed rail.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They ought to be engaged in breaking ground in other technologies, doing waste recycling, clean water technology and things of that kind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can create millions of jobs in these new technologies- -more than we’re going to lose in defense — if we target it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we’re investing a much smaller percentage of our income in the things you just asked about than all of our major competitors, and our wealth growth is going down as a result of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s making the country poorer, which is why I answered the gentleman the way I did before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to both bring down the deficit and get our economy going through these kinds of investments in order to get the kind of wealth and jobs and incomes we need in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: First you’ve got to have money to pay for these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So you’ve got to create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There are all kinds of ways to create jobs in the inner city.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m not a politician, but I think I could go to Washington in a week and get everybody holding hands and get this bill signed because I talk to the Democratic leaders and they want it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I talk to the Republican leaders and they want it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But since they’re bred from childhood to fight with one another rather than get results, you know, I would be glad to drop out and spend a little time and see if we couldn’t build some bridges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, results is what counts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The president can’t order Congress around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Congress can’t order the president around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s not bad for a guy that’s never been there, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But you have to work together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, I have talked to the chairmen of the committees that want this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The president wants it, but we can’t get it because we sit here in gridlock because it’s a campaign year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t fund a lot of other things this year, like the savings and loan mess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s another story that we’re going to pay a big price for right after the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The facts are though — the facts are — the American people are hurting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These people are hurting in the inner cities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re shipping the quote, “low paying jobs” overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: What are low paying jobs?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Textiles, shoes, things like that that we say are yesterday’s industries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re tomorrow’s industries in the inner cities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let me say in my case, if I’m out of work, I’ll cut grass tomorrow to take care of my family; I’ll be happy to make shoes, I’ll be happy to make clothing, I’ll make sausage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You just give me a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Put those jobs in the inner cities instead of doing diplomatic deals and shipping them to China where prison labor does the work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you ask me if I could fly a fighter plane or be an astronaut, I can’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve spent my life creating jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s something I know how to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And, very simply, in the inner city, they’re starved — you see, small business is the way to jump start the inner city, not —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You want jobs in the inner city?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Do you want jobs in the inner city?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Is that your question?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Oh, I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve listened to both sides, and if they would talk to one another instead of throwing rocks, I think we could get a lot done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And, among other things, I would say, okay, over here in this Senate committee to the chairman who is anxious to get this bill passed, the president who is anxious, I’d say rather than just yelling at one another, why don’t we find out where we’re apart, try to get together, get the bill passed and give the people the benefits and not play party politics right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I think the press would follow that so closely that probably they would get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way I would do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I doubt if they’ll give me the chance, but I will drop everything and go work on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I support the right to keep and bear arms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I live in a state where over half the adults have hunting or fishing licenses, or both.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I believe we have to have some way of checking hand guns before they’re sold, to check the criminal history, the mental health history, and the age of people who are buying them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Therefore I support the Brady bill which would impose a national waiting period unless and until a state did what only Virginia has done now, which is to automate its records.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Once you automate your records, then you don’t have to have a waiting period, but at least you can check.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also think we should have frankly restrictions on assault weapons whose only purpose is to kill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to give the police a fighting chance in our urban areas where the gangs are building up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The third thing I would say — it doesn’t bear directly on gun control, but it’s very important — we need more police on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There is a crime bill which would put more police on the street, which was killed for this session by a filibuster in the Senate, mostly be Republican senators, and I think it’s a shame it didn’t pass, I think it should be made the law — but it had the Brady bill in it, the waiting period.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also believe that we should offer college scholarships to people who will agree to work them off as police officers, and I think, as we reduce our military forces, we should let people earn military retirement by coming out and working as police officers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thirty years ago there were three police officers on the street for every crime; today there are three crimes for every police officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In the communities which have had real success putting police officers near schools where kids carry weapons, to get the weapons out of the schools, are on the same blocks, you’ve seen crime go down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In Houston there’s been a 15- percent drop in the crime rate in the last year because of the work the mayor did there in increasing the police force.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I know it can work; I’ve seen it happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think you put your finger on a major problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I talk about strengthening the American family and it’s very hard to strengthen the family if people are scared to walk down to the corner store and, you know, send their kid down to get a loaf of bread.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s very hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have been fighting for very strong anti-crime legislation — habeas corpus reform, so you don’t have these endless appeals, so when somebody gets sentenced, hey, this is for real.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been fighting for changes in the exclusionary rule so if an honest cop stops somebody and makes a technical mistake, the criminal doesn’t go away.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll probably get into a fight in this room with some but I happen to think that we need stronger death penalties for those that kill police officers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Virginia’s in the lead in this, as Governor Clinton properly said, on this identification system for firearms.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am not for national registration of firearms.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some of the states that have the toughest anti-gun laws have the highest levels of crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am for the right, as the governor says- -I’m a sportsman and I don’t think you ought to eliminate all kinds of weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I was not for the bill that he was talking about because it was not tough enough on the criminal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m very pleased that the Fraternal Order of Police in Little Rock, Arkansas endorsed me because I think they see I’m trying to strengthen the anti-crime legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got more money going out for local police than any previous administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to get it under control and there’s one last point I’d make.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have got to win our national strategy against drugs, the fight against drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re making some progress, doing a little better on interdiction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re not doing as well amongst the people that get to be habitual drug-users.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The good news is, and I think it’s true in Richmond, teenage use is down of cocaine, substantially, 60% in the last couple of years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’re making progress but until we get that one done, we’re not going to solve the neighborhood crime problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t get to make a comment on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Oh, you’re going to let me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: On any program, and this includes crime, you’ll find we have all kinds of great plans lying around that never get enacted into law and implemented.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t care what it is — competitiveness, health care, crime, you name it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Brady Bill, I agree that it’s a timid step in the right direction but it won’t fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So why pass a law that won’t fix it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, what it really boils down to is can you live — we become so preoccupied with the rights of the criminal that we’ve forgotten the rights of the innocent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And in our country we have evolved to a point where we’ve put millions of innocent people in jail because you go to the poor neighborhoods and they’ve put bars on their windows and bars on their doors and put themselves in jail to protect the things that they acquired legitimately.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s where we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have got to become more concerned about people who play by the rules and get the balance we require.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is going to take first, building a consensus at grassroots America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Right from the bottom up, the American people have got to say they want it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And at that point, we can pick from a variety of plans and develop new plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the way you get things done is bury yourselves in the room with one another, put together the best program, take it to the American people, use the electronic town hall, the kind of thing you’re doing here tonight, build a consensus and then do it and then go on to the next one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But don’t just sit here slow dancing for 4 years doing nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Any order?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll be glad to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I strongly support term limits for members of the US Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe it would return the government closer to the people, the way that Ross Perot is talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The president’s terms are limited to 2, a total of 8 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s wrong with limiting the terms of members of Congress to 12?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Congress has gotten kind of institutionalized.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For 38 years one party has controlled the House of Representatives, and the result, a sorry little post office that can’t do anything right and a bank that has more overdrafts than all the Chase Bank and Citibank put together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do something about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think you get a certain arrogance, bureaucratic arrogance, if people stay there too long.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I favor, strongly favor, term limits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And how to get them passed?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Send us some people that will pass the idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think you will.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people want it now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Every place I go I talk about it, and I think they want it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Actually, you’d have to have some amendments to the Constitution because of the way the Constitution reads.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know they’re popular, but I’m against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe, number one, it would pose a real problem for a lot of smaller states in the Congress who have enough trouble now making sure their interests are heard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 2, I think it would increase the influence of unelected staff members in the Congress who have too much influence already.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to cut the size of the congressional staffs, but I think you’re going to have too much influence there with people who were never elected, who have lots of expertise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 3, if the people really have a mind to change, they can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to have 120 to 150 new members of Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me tell you what I favor instead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I favor strict controls on how much you can spend running for Congress, strict limits on political action committees, requirements that people running for Congress appear in open public debates like we’re doing now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you did that you could take away the incumbents’ advantage because challengers like me would have a chance to run against incumbents like him for House races and Senate races, and then the voters could make up their own mind without being subject to an unfair fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So that’s how I feel about it, and I think if we had the right kind of campaign reform, we’d get the changes you want.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let me do first on a personal level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If the American people send me up to do this job, I intend to be there one term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I do not intend to spend one minute of one day thinking about re-election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And as a matter of principle — and my situation is unique, and I understand it — I would take absolutely no compensation; I go as their servant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, I have set as strong an example as I can, then at that point when we sit down over at Capitol Hill — tomorrow night I’m going to be talking about government reform — it’s a long subject, you wouldn’t let me finish tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you want to hear it, you get it tomorrow night — you’ll hear it tomorrow night.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But we have got to reform government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you put term limits in and don’t reform government, you won’t get the benefits you thought.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It takes both.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we need to do the reforms and the term limits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And after we reform it, it won’t be a lifetime career opportunity; good people will go serve and then go back to their homes and not become foreign lobbyists and cash in at 30,000 bucks a month and then take time off to run some president’s campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re all nice people, they’re just in a bad system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there are any villains, but, boy, is the system rotten.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had more people talk to me about their health care problems I guess than anything else, all across America — you know, people who’ve lost their jobs, lost their businesses, had to give up their jobs because of sick children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So let me try to answer you in this way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s start with a premise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We spend 30% more of our income than any nation on earth on health care, and yet we insure fewer people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have 35 million people without any insurance at all — and I see them all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A hundred thousand Americans a month have lost their health insurance just in the last 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So if you analyze where we’re out of line with other countries, you come up with the following conclusions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number one, we spend at least $60 billion a year on insurance, administrative cost, bureaucracy, and government regulation that wouldn’t be spent in any other nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we have to have, in my judgment, a drastic simplification of the basic health insurance policies of this country, be very comprehensive for everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Employers would cover their employees, government would cover the unemployed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 2, I think you have to take on specifically the insurance companies and require them to make some significant change in the way they rate people in the big community pools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to tell the pharmaceutical companies they can’t keep raising drug prices at three times the rate of inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to take on medical fraud.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to help doctors stop practicing defensive medicine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve recommended that our doctors be given a set of national practice guidelines and that if they follow those guidelines that raises the presumption that they didn’t do anything wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think you have to have a system of primary and preventive clinics in our inner cities and our rural areas so people can have access to health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The key is to control the cost and maintain the quality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: To do that you need a system of managed competition where all of us are covered in big groups and we can choose our doctors and our hospitals, a wide range, but there is an incentive to control costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think there has to be — I think Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot and I agree on this, there has to be a national commission of health care providers and health care consumers that set ceilings to keep health costs in line with inflation, plus population growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me say, some people say we can’t do this but Hawaii does it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They cover 98% of their people and their insurance premiums are much cheaper than the rest of America, and so does Rochester, New York.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They now have a plan to cover everybody and their premiums are two-thirds of the rest of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a big human problem and a devastating economic problem for America, and I’m going to send a plan to do this within the first 100 days of my presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s terribly important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just have to say something.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to stampede.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ross was very articulate across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want anybody to stampede to cut the president’s salary off altogether.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Barbara’s sitting over here and I — but what I have proposed, 10% cut, downsize the government, and we can get that done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: She asked a question, I think, is whether the health care profession was to blame.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One thing to blame is these malpractice lawsuits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re breaking the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It costs $20-25 billion a year, and I want to see those outrageous claims capped.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Doctors don’t dare to deliver babies sometimes because they’re afraid that somebody’s going to sue them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People don’t dare — medical practitioners, to help somebody along the highway that are hurt because they’re afraid that some lawyer’s going to come along and get a big lawsuit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So you can’t blame the practitioners for the health problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And my program is this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Keep the government as far out of it as possible, make insurance available to the poorest of the poor, through vouchers, next range in the income bracket, through tax credits, and get on about the business of pooling insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A great big company can buy — Ross has got a good-sized company, been very successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He can buy insurance cheaper than Mom and Pop’s store on the corner.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if those Mom and Pop stores all get together and pool, they too can bring the cost of insurance down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I want to keep the quality of health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That means keep government out of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to do — I don’t like this idea of these boards.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It all sounds to me like you’re going to have some government setting price.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want competition and I want to pool the insurance and take care of it that way and have — oh, here’s the other point.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think medical care should go with the person.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you leave a business, I think your insurance should go with you to some other business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You shouldn’t be worrying if you get a new job as to whether that’s gonna — and part of our plan is to make it what they call portable — big word, but that means if you’re working for the Jones Company and you go to the Smith Company, your insurance goes with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s a good program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m really excited about getting it done, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have the most expensive health care system in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Twelve percent of our gross national product goes to health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our industrial competitors, who are beating us in competition, spend less and have better health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Japan spends a little over 6% of its gross national product.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Germany spends 8%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s fascinating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve bought a front row box seat and you’re not happy with your health care and you’re saying tonight we’ve got bad health care but very expensive health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Folks, here’s why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Go home and look in the mirror.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You own this country but you have no voice in it the way it’s organized now, and if you want to have a high risk experience, comparable to bungee jumping, go into Congress some time when they’re working on this kind of legislation, when the lobbyists are running up and down the halls.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Wear your safety toe shoes when you go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And as a private citizen, believe me, you are looked on as a major nuisance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The facts are you now have a government that comes at you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’re supposed to have a government that comes from you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, there are all kinds of good ideas, brilliant ideas, terrific ideas on health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: None of them ever get implemented because — let me give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A senator runs every 6 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: He’s got to raise 20,000 bucks a week to have enough money to run.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who’s he gonna listen to — us or the folks running up and down the aisles with money, the lobbyists, the PAC money?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: He listens to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who do they represent?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Health care industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Not us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, you’ve got to have a government that comes from you again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to reassert your ownership in this country and you’ve got to completely reform our government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And at that point they’ll just be like apples falling out of a tree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The programs will be good because the elected officials will be listening to — I said the other night I was all ears and I would listen to any good idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to do plastic surgery on a lot of these guys so that they’re all ears, too, and listen to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then you get what you want, and shouldn’t you?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You paid for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Why shouldn’t you get what you want, as opposed to what some lobbyist cuts a deal, writes a little piece in the law and he goes through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way the game’s played now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Till you change it you’re gonna be unhappy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: SIMPSON : You wanted one brief point in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One brief point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have elections so people can make decisions about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The point I want to make to you is, a bipartisan commission reviewed my plan and the Bush plan and there were as many Republicans as Democratic health care experts on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They concluded that my plan would cover everybody and his would leave 27 million behind by the year 2000 and that my plan in the next 12 years would save $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 2 trillion in public and private money to reinvest in this economy and the average family would save $1200 a year under the plan that I offered without any erosion in the quality of health care So I ask you to look at that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you have to vote for somebody with a plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what you have elections for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If people would say, well, he got elected to do this and then the Congress says, okay, I’m going to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what the election was about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: END of first half of 1992 Debate 2 October 15, 1992 Second Half Debate Transcript October 15, 1992 The Second Clinton-Bush-Perot Presidential Debate This is the second half of the transcript of the Richmond debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The October 15th “town hall” format debate was moderated by Carole Simpson.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The length of this printed transcript is approximately 20 pages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: May I answer that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who do you want to start with?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It caused me to disrupt my private life and my business to get involved in this activity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s how much I care about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And believe me, if you knew my family and if you knew the private life I have, you would agree in a minute that that’s a whole lot more fun than getting involved in politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But I have lived the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I came from very modest background.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Nobody’s been luckier than I’ve been, all the way across the spectrum, and the greatest riches of all are my wife and children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s true of any family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But I want all the children — I want these young people up here to be able to start with nothing but an idea like I did and build a business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But they’ve got to have a strong basic economy and if you’re in debt, it’s like having a ball and chain around you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I just figure, as lucky as I’ve been, I owe it to them and I owe it to the future generations and on a very personal basis, I owe it to my children and grandchildren.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think the national debt affects everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Obviously it has a lot to do with interest rates —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure it has.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I love my grandchildren —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to think that they’re going to be able to afford an education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that that’s an important part of being a parent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If the question — maybe I — get it wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Are you suggesting that if somebody has means that the national debt doesn’t affect them?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not sure I get — help me with the question and I’ll try to answer it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, listen, you ought to be in the White House for a day and hear what I hear and see what I see and read the mail I read and touch the people that I touch from time to time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was in the Lomax AME Church.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a black church just outside of Washington, DC.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I read in the bulletin about teenage pregnancies, about the difficulties that families are having to make ends meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I talk to parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you’ve got to care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everybody cares if people aren’t doing well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think it’s fair to say, you haven’t had cancer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Therefore, you don’t know what’s it like.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s fair to say, you know, whatever it is, that if you haven’t been hit by it personally.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
