transcript_turns.text: But everybody’s affected by the debt because of the tremendous interest that goes into paying on that debt everything’s more expensive.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everything comes out of your pocket and my pocket.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So it’s that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think in terms of the recession, of course you feel it when you’re president of the US.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I’m trying to do something about it by stimulating the export, vesting more, better education systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m glad you clarified it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Tell me how it’s affected you again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know people who’ve lost their jobs and lost their homes?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve been governor of a small state for 12 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you how it’s affected me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Every year Congress and the president sign laws that make us do more things and gives us less money to do it with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I see people in my state, middle class people — their taxes have gone up in Washington and their services have gone down while the wealthy have gotten tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have seen what’s happened in this last 4 years when — in my state, when people lose their jobs there’s a good chance I’ll know them by their names.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When a factory closes, I know the people who ran it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When the businesses go bankrupt, I know them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been out here for 13 months meeting in meetings just like this ever since October, with people like you all over America, people that have lost their jobs, lost their livelihood, lost their health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What I want you to understand is the national debt is not the only cause of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is because America has not invested in its people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is because we have not grown.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is because we’ve had 12 years of trickle down economics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gone from first to twelfth in the world in wages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had 4 years where we’ve produced no private sector jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Most people are working harder for less money than they were making ten years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is because we are in the grip of a failed economic theory.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And this decision you’re about to make better be about what kind of economic theory you want, not just people saying I’m going to go fix it but what are we going to do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we have to do is invest in American jobs, American education, control American health care costs and bring the American people together again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the Social Security — you’re an expert and I could, I’m sure, learn from you the details of the Pension Guarantee Fund and the Social Security Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Social Security system was fixed about 5 years, and I think it’s projected out to be sound beyond that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So at least we have time to work with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But on all of these things, a sound economy is the only way to get it going.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Growth in the economy is gonna add to the overall prosperity and wealth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t give you a specific answer on Pension Guarantee Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All I know is that we have firm government credit to guarantee the pensions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that is very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s — the full faith and credit of the US, in spite of our difficulties, is still pretty good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s still the most respected credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I would simply say, as these dates get close, you’re going to have to reorganize and refix as we did with the Social Security Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s the only answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the more immediate answer is to do what this lady was suggesting we do, and that is to get this deficit down and get on without adding to the woes, and then restructure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One thing I’ve called for that has been stymied, and I’ll keep on working for it, is a whole financial reform legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is absolutely essential in terms of bringing our banking system and credit system into the new age instead of having it living back in the dark ages.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a big fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t want to give my friend Ross another shot at me here but I am fighting with the Congress to get this through.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you can’t just go up and say I’m going to fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got some pretty strong-willed guys up there that argue with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But that’s what the election’s about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I agree with the governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what the election’s about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And sound fiscal policy is the best answer, I think, to all the three problems you mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: On the broad issue here, when you’re trying to solve a problem, you get the best plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You have a raging debate about those plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then out of that debate, with leadership, comes consensus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then, if the plans are huge and complex like health care, I would urge you to implement pilot programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Like the old carpenter says measure twice, cut once.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s make sure this thing’s as good as we all think it is at the end of the meeting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then finally, our government passes laws and freezes the plan in concrete.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Anybody that’s ever built a successful business will tell you you optimize, optimize, optimize after you’ve put something into effect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The reason Medicare and Medicaid are a mess is we froze them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Everybody knows how to fix them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There are people all over the federal government, if they could just touch it with a screwdriver, could fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, back over here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, we’ve got a $4 trillion debt and only in America would you have $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 8 trillion of it or 70% of it financed 5 years or less.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s another thing for you to think about when you go home tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You don’t finance long-term debt with short-term money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Why did our government do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: To get the interest rates down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A 1% increase in interest rates in that $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 8 trillion is $28 billion a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, when you look at what Germany pays for money and what we don’t pay for money, you realize there’s quite a spread, right, and you realize this is a temporary thing and there’s going to be another sucking sound that runs our deficit through the roof.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You know, and everybody’s ducking it so I’m gonna say it, that we are not letting that surplus stay in the bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We are not investing that surplus like a pension fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We are spending that surplus to make the deficit look smaller to you than it really is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, that — put you in jail in corporate America if you kept books that way but in government it’s just kind of the way things are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s because it comes at you, not from you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now then, that money needs to be — they don’t even pay interest on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They just write a note for the interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Do you want to fix the problem or sound-bite it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I understand the importance of time but see, here’s how we get to this mess we’re in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is just 1 of 1000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now then, to nail it, there’s one way out — a growing, expanding job base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A growing, expanding job base to generate the funds and the tax revenues to pay off the mess and rebuild America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to double-hit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If we’re $4 trillion down, we should have everything perfect, but we don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to pay it off and build money to renew it- -spend money to renew it, and that’s going to take a growing, expanding job base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That is priority one in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Put everybody that’s breathing to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I’d love to be out of workers and have to import them, like some of our international competitors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I apologize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think I remember the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say first of all, I want to answer your specific question but first of all, we all agree that there should be a growing economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What you have to decide is who’s got the best economic plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we all have ideas out there, and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush has a record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t want you to read my lips and I sure don’t want you to read his.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I do hope you will read our plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, specifically, one, on Medicare, it is not true that everyone knows how to fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are different ideas — the Bush plan, the Perot plan, the Clinton — we have different ideas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am convinced, having studied health care for a year hard and talking to hundreds and hundreds of people all across America, that you cannot control the cost of Medicare until you control the cost of private health care and public health care, with managed competition, ceiling on cost, and radical reorganization of the insurance markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to do that; we got to get those costs down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 2, with regard to Social Security, that program — a lot of you may not know this — it produces a $70 billion surplus a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Social Security is in surplus $70 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Six increases in the payroll tax — that means people with incomes of $51,000 a year or less pay a disproportionally high share of the federal tax burden, which is why I want some middle-class tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What do we have to do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: By the time the century turns, we have got to have our deficit under control, we have to work out of so that surplus is building up so when the baby boomers like me retire, we’re okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 3, on the pension funds, I don’t know as much about it, but I will say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What I would do is to bring in the pension experts of the country, take a look at it, and strengthen the pension requirements further, because it’s not just enough to have the guarantee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We had a guarantee on the S&Ls, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We had a guarantee — and what happened?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You picked up a $500-billion bill because of the dumb way the federal government deregulated it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think we are going to have to change and strengthen the pension requirements on private retirement plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, we have come to that position.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Since I became president, 43, 44 countries have gone democratic, no longer totalitarian, no longer living under dictatorship or communist rule.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is exciting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: New world order to me means freedom and democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we will have a continuing responsibility, as the only remaining superpower, to stay involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we pull back in some isolation and say we don’t have to do our share, or more than our share, anymore, I believe you are going to just ask for conflagration that we’ll get involved in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: NATO, for example, has kept the peace for many, many years, and I want to see us keep fully staffed in NATO so we’ll continue to guarantee the peace in Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the exciting thing is, the fear of nuclear war is down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you hear all the bad stuff that’s happened on my watch; I hope people will recognize that this is something pretty good for mankind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope they’ll think it’s good that democracy and freedom is on the move.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to stay engaged, as long as I’m president, working to improve things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, it’s so easy now to say, hey, cut out foreign aid, we got a problem at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the US has to still have the Statue of Liberty as a symbol, caring for others.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Right this very minute we’re sending supplies in to help these little starving kids in Somalia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the US that’s taken the lead in humanitarian aid into Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing this all around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we got problems at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think I got a good plan to help fix those problems at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But because of our leadership, because we didn’t listen to the freeze — the nuclear-freeze group, do you remember — freeze it, back in the late 70s — freeze, don’t touch it; we’re going to lock it in now or else we’ll have war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: President Reagan said no, peace through strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Soviet Union is no more, and now we’re working to help them become totally democratic through the Freedom Support Act that I led on, a great Democratic ambassador, Bob Strauss, over there, Jim Baker, all of us got this thing passed — through cooperation, Ross — it worked with cooperation, and you’re for that, I’m sure, helping Russia become democratic.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So the new world order to me means freedom and democracy, keep engaged, do not pull back into isolation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we are the US, and we have a responsibility to lead and to guarantee the security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If it hadn’t been for us, Saddam Hussein would be sitting on top of three-fifths of the oil supply of the world and he’d have nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And only the US could do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me, Carole.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s cost-effective to help Russia succeed in its revolution; it’s pennies on the dollar compared to going back to the Cold War.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Russia is still very unstable; they could go back to square one, and worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: All the nuclear weapons are not dismantled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I am particularly concerned about the intercontinental weapons, the ones that can hit us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got agreements, but they are still there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: With all this instability and breaking into republics, and all the Middle Eastern countries going over there and shopping for weapons, we’ve got our work cut out for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we need to stay right on top of that and constructively help them move toward democracy and capitalism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have to have money to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have to have our people at work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, for 45 years we were preoccupied with the Red Army.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I suggest now that our number one preoccupation is red ink and our country and we’ve got to put our people back to work so that we can afford to do these things we want to do in Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We cannot be the policeman for the world any longer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We spent $300 billion a year defending the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Germany and Japan spend around $30 billion a piece.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If I can get you to defend me and I can spend all my money building industry that’s a home run for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Coming out of World War II it made sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, the other superpowers need to do their part.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll close on this point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You can’t be a superpower unless you’re an economic superpower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If we’re not an economic superpower, we’re a used to be and we will no longer be a force for good throughout the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if nothing else gets you excited about rebuilding our industrial base maybe that will because job one is to put our people back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d rather answer her question first and then I’ll be glad to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because the question you ask is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The end of the Cold War brings an incredible opportunity for change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Winds of freedom blowing around the world, Russia demilitarizing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it also requires us to maintain some continuity — some bipartisan American commitment to certain principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I would just say there are three things that I would like to say — number one — we do have to maintain the world’s strongest defense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We may differ about what the elements of that are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that defense needs to be — with fewer people in permanent armed services but with greater mobility on the land, in the air and on the sea, with a real dedication to continuing development of high technology weaponry and well trained people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we’re going to have to work to stop the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Got to keep going until all those nuclear weapons in Russia are gone and the other republics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 2, if you don’t rebuild the economic strength of this country at home, we won’t be a superpower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can’t have any more instances like what happened when Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush went to Japan and the Japanese prime minister said he felt sympathy for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to be the strongest economic power in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what got me into this race, so we could rebuild the American economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And number three, we need to be a force for freedom and democracy and we need to use our unique position to support freedom, whether it’s in Haiti or in China or in any other place, wherever the seeds of freedom are sprouting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can’t impose it, but we need to nourish it and that’s the kind of thing that I would do as president — follow those three commitments into the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Go ahead, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, go ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d be delighted to, because you can’t do it the old way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do it with the school bureaucracy controlling everything and that’s why we have a new program that I hope people have heard about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s being worked now in 1700 communities — bypassed Congress on this one, Ross — 1700 communities across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s called America 2000.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it literally says to the communities, re-invent the schools, not just the bricks and mortar but the curriculum and everything else.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Think anew.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a concept called the New American School Corporation where we’re doing exactly that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I believe that we’ve got to get the power in the hands of the teachers, not the teachers’ union.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s happening up there?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so our America 2000 program also says this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says let’s give parents the choice of a public, private or public school — public, private or religious school.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it works- -it works in Milwaukee.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Democratic woman up there — taking the lead in this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The mayor up there, on the program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the schools that are not chosen are improved — competition does that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to innovate through school choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to innovate through this America 2000 program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But she is absolutely right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The programs that we’ve been trying where you control everything and mandate it from Washington don’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The governors — and I believe Governor Clinton was in on this — but maybe — I don’t want to invoke him here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But they come to me and they say, please get the Congress to stop passing so many mandates telling us how to control things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We know better how to do it in California or Texas or wherever it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So this is what our program is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe you’re right on to something, that if we don’t change the education we’re not going to be able to compete.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Federal funding for education is up substantially — Pell grants are up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it isn’t going to get the job done if we don’t change K through 12.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, let me say that I’ve spent more of my time and life on this in the last 12 years than any other issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Seventy percent of my state’s money goes to the public schools, and I was really honored when Time magazine said that our schools have shown more improvement than any other state in the country except one other — they named 2 states showing real strides forward in the 80s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I care a lot about this, and I’ve spent countless hours in schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let me start with what you said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with some of what Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush said, but it’s nowhere near enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We live in a world where what you earn depends on what you can learn, where the average 18- year-old will change jobs 8 times in a lifetime and where none of us can promise any of you that what you now do for a living is absolutely safe from now on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Nobody running can promise that, there’s too much change in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So what should we do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me reel some things off real quick, because you said you wanted specifics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number one, under my program we would provide matching funds to states to teach everybody with a job to read in the next 5 years and give everybody with a job the chance to get a high school diploma, in big places on the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 2, we would provide 2-year apprenticeship programs to high school graduates who don’t go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And community colleges are on the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we’d open the doors to college education to high school graduates without regard to income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They could borrow the money and pay it back as a percentage of their income or with a couple of years of service to our nation here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number 4, we would fully fund the Head Start program to get little kids off to a good start.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, 5, I would have an aggressive program of school reform, more choices — I favor public schools or these new charter schools — we can talk about that if you want.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we should spend tax money on private schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I favor public school choice, and I favor radical decentralization in giving more power to better-trained principals and teachers with parent councils to control their schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those things would revolutionize American education and take us to the top economically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In 6 years — I budget all this in my budget, and in 6 years the college program would cost 8 billion dollars over and above what — the present student loan program costs 4; you pay 3 billion dollars for busted loans, because we don’t have an automatic recovery system, and a billion dollars in bank fees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So the net cost would be 8 billion 6 years from now in a trillion-plus budget — not very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The other stuff — all the other stuff I mentioned — costs much less than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Head Start program full funding would cost about 5 billion more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it’s all covered in my budget from — the plans that I’ve laid out — from raising taxes on families with incomes above $200,000 and asking foreign corporations to pay the same tax that American corporations do on the same income, from $140 billion in budget cuts, including what I think are very prudent cuts in the defense budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s all covered in the plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I’ve got scars to show for being around education reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the first word you need to say in every city and state, and just draw a line in the sand, is public schools exist for the benefit of the children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to see a lot of people fall over it, because any time you’re spending $199 billion dollars a year, somebody’s getting it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the children get lost in the process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So that’s step one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Keep in mind in 1960, when our schools were the envy of the world, we were spending $16 billion on them; now we spend more than any other nation in the world — 199 billion a year — and rank at the bottom of the industrialized world in terms of education achievement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One more time you’ve bought a front-row box seat and got a third-rate performance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is a government that is not serving you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: By and large it should be local — the more local, the better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Interesting phenomenon: small towns have good schools, big cities have terrible schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The best people in a small town will serve on the school board; you get into big cities, it’s political patronage, stepping stones — you get the job, give your relatives a janitor’s job at $57,000 a year, more than the teachers make, and with luck they clean the cafeteria once a week.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, you’re paying for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Those schools belong to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we put up with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, as long as we put up with that, that’s what you’re going to get.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And these folks are just dividing up 199 billion bucks and the children get lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If I could wish for one thing for great public schools, it would be a strong family unit in every home — nothing will ever replace that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You say, well, gee, what are you going to do about that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, the White House is a bully pulpit, and I think we ought to be pounding on the table every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There’s nothing — the most efficient unit of government the world will ever know is a strong loving family unit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Next thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You need small schools, not big schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In a little school everybody is somebody; individualism is very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These big factories?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Everybody told me they were cost-effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I did a study on it; they’re cost- ineffective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 5000 students — why is a high school that big?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One reason.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Sooner or later you get 11 more boys that can run like the devil that weigh 250 pounds and they might win district.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, that has nothing to do with learning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, across Texas, typically half of the school day was non-academic pursuits — in one place it was 35%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In Texas you could have unlimited absences to go to livestock shows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Found a boy — excuse me, but this gives the flavor — a boy in Houston kept a chicken in the bathtub in downtown Houston and missed 65 days going to livestock shows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Finally had to come back to school, the chicken lost its feathers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s the only way we got him back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s your tax money being wasted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, neighborhood schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It is terrible to bus tiny little children across town.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it is particularly terrible to take poor tiny little children and wait until the first grade and bus them across town to Mars, where the children know their numbers, know their letters, have had every advantage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: At the end of the first day, that little child wants out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll close on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to have world class teachers, world class books.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you ever got close to how textbooks were selected, you wouldn’t want to go back the second day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have time to tell you the stories.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Finally, if we don’t fix this, you’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We can’t have the industries of tomorrow unless we have the best educated workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And here you’ve got, for the disadvantaged children, you’ve got to have early childhood development.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Cheapest money you’ll ever spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: First contact should be with the money when she’s pregnant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That little child needs to be loved and hugged and nurtured and made to feel special, like your children were.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They learn to think well or poorly of themselves in the first 18 months.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And in the first few years they either learn how to learn or don’t learn how to learn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if they don’t, they wind up in prison.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it costs more to keep them in prison than it does to send them to Harvard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I rest my case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just had a word of clarification because of something Governor Clinton said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My school choice program, GI Bill for Kids, does not take public money and give it to private schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It does what the GI Bill itself did when I came out of World War II.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It takes public money and gives it to families or individuals to choose the school they want.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And where it’s been done, those schools, like in Rochester, those schools that weren’t chosen find that they then compete and do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I think it’s worth a shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a pilot program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It ought to be tried.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: School choice — public, private or religious.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not to the schools but to — you know, 46% of the teachers in Chicago, public school teachers, send their kids to private school.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think we ought to try to help families and see if it will do what I think — make all schools better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I just want to mention if I could —

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Very briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Including the parents in the preschool education of their kids, even if they’re poor and uneducated, can make a huge difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have a big program in my state that teaches mothers or fathers to teach their kids to get ready for school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s the most successful thing we’ve ever done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Just a fact clarification real quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We do not spend a higher percentage of our income on public education than every other country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are 9 countries that spend more than we do on public education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We spend more on education ’cause we spend so much more on colleges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But if you look at public education alone and you take into account the fact that we have more racial diversity and more poverty, it makes a big difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are great public schools where there’s public school choice, accountability and brilliant principals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll just mention one — the Beasley Academic Center in Chicago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I commend it to anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s as good as any private school in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t have any idea but I hope it will happen some time in my lifetime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe that this country is electing more and more African Americans and Latinos and Asian Americans who are representing districts that are themselves not necessarily of a majority of their race.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The American people are beginning to vote across racial lines, and I hope it will happen more and more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: More and more women are being elected.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at all these women Senate candidates we have here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you know, according to my mother and my wife and my daughter, this world would be a lot better place if women were running it most of the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I do think there are special experiences and judgments and backgrounds and understandings that women bring to this process, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This lady said here, how have you been affected by the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I mean, women know what’s it like to be paid an unequal amount for equal work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They know what it’s like not to have flexible working hours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They know what it’s like not to have family leave or childcare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think it would be a good thing for America if it happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think it will happen in my lifetime.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think if Barbara Bush were running this year she’d be elected.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s too late.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You don’t want us to mention appointees, but when you see the quality of people in our administration, see how Colin Powell performed — I say administration —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You weren’t impressed with the fact that he —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, but wouldn’t that suggest to the American people, then, here’s a quality person, if he decided that he could automatically get the nomination of either party?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Huh?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Oh, I see.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You mean, time?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know — starting after 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I think you’ll see —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think you’ll see more minority candidates and women candidates coming forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is supposed to be the year of the women in the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s see how they do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope a lot of —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I have a fearless forecast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A message just won’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Colin Powell will be on somebody’s ticket 4 years from now — right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: He wanted that said — 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if won’t be, General Waller would be — you say, why do you keep picking military people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These are people that I just happen to know and have a high regard for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure there are hundreds of others.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: How about Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Lou Sullivan?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, a good man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Oh, oh.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: totally agree.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My candidate’s back there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I can think of many.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: How about Sandra Day O’Connor as an example?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Bernadine Healy —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: National Institutes of Health.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll yield the floor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All good Republicans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Name some more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: May I ask for an exception because I think we owe Carole Simpson — anybody who can stand in between these three characters here and get the job done — we owe her a round of applause.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But don’t take it out of my time!

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I feel strongly about it because I don’t want it to come out of my time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, but let me just stay to the American people in 2 and a half weeks we’re going to choose who should sit in this Oval Office, who to lead the economic recovery, who to be the leader of the free world, who to get the deficit down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: three ways to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One is to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One is to reduce spending — controlling that mandatory spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Another one is to invest and save and to stimulate growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do not want to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I differ with the 2 here on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m just not going to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do believe that we need to control mandatory spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to invest and save more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we need to educate better and retrain better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we need to export more so I’ll keep working for export agreements where we can sell more abroad and I believe that we must strengthen the family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to strengthen the family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me pose this question to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If in the next 5 minutes a television announcer came on and said, there is a major international crisis — there is a major threat to the world or in this country a major threat — my question is, who, if you were appointed to name 1 of the 3 of us, who would you choose?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Who has the perseverance, the character, the integrity, the maturity, to get the job done?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope I’m that person.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very, very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If the American people want to do it and not talk about it, then they ought to — you know, I’m one person they ought to consider.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If they just want to keep slow dancing and talk about it and not do it, I’m not your man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I am results oriented.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I am action oriented.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve dealt my businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Getting things done in three months that my competitors took 18 months to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Everybody says you can’t do that with Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Sure, you can do that with Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Congress — they’re all good people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re all patriots but you’ve got to link arms and work with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Sure, you’ll have arguments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Sure, you’ll have fights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have them all day every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But we get the job done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, I have to come back in my clothes to one thing because I am passionate about education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I was talking about early childhood education for disadvantaged little children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And let me tell you one specific pilot program where children who don’t have a chance go to this program when they’re 3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now we’re going back to when the mother’s pregnant and they’ll start right after they’re born.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Starting when they’re 3 and going to this school until they’re 9 and then going into the public school in the 4th grade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Ninety percent are on the honor role.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now that will change America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Those children will all go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They will live the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I beg the American people, any time they think about reforming education to take this piece of society that doesn’t have a chance and take these little pieces of clay that can be shaped and molded and give them the same love and nurture and affection and support you give your children and teach them that they’re unique and that they’re precious and that there’s only one person in the world like them and you will see this nation bloom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we will have so many people who are qualified for the top job that it will be terrific.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, finally, if you can’t pay the bills you’re dead in the water.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we have got to put our nation back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you don’t want to really do that I’m not your man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d go crazy sitting up there slow dancing that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In other words, unless we’re going to do it, then pick somebody who likes to talk about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, just remember when you think about me — I didn’t create this mess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been paying taxes just like you and Lord knows, I’ve paid my share — over a billion in taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And for a guy that started out with everything he owned in the trunk of his car —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: — that ain’t bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But it’s in your hands.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I wish you well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll see you tomorrow night — on NBC — 10:30 to 11:00 Eastern Time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Carole, and thank you, ladies and gentlemen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Since I suggested this format I hope it’s been good for all of you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I really tried to be faithful to your request that we answer the questions specifically and pointedly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I thought I owed that to you and I respect you for being here and for the impact you’ve had on making this a more positive experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: These problems are not easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’re not going to be solved overnight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I want you to think about just 2 or 3 things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, the people of my state have let me be their governor for 12 years because I made commitments to 2 things — more jobs and better schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our schools are now better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our children get off to a better start from pre-school programs and smaller classes in the early grades, and we have one of the most aggressive adult education programs in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We talked about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This year my state ranks first in the country in job growth, 4th in manufacturing in job growth, 4th in income growth, 4th in the decline of poverty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It happened because I could work with people — Republicans and Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’ve had 24 retired generals and admirals, hundreds of business people, many of them Republican, support this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You have to decide whether you want to change or not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We do not need 4 more years of an economic theory that doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had 12 years of trickle down economics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to put the American people first, to invest and grow this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m the only person here who’s ever balanced a government budget and I’ve presented 12 of them and cut spending repeatedly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But you cannot just get there by balancing the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to grow the economy by putting people first — real people like you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I got into this race because I did not want my child to grow up to be part of the first generation of Americans to do worse than her parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re better than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can do better than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to make America as great as it can be and I ask for your help in doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.
